headline.purpose: Section h2, always followed by the tick-rule and a lead.

title.purpose: h3s in lists, steps, offers, form heading; phone numbers with tabular numerals.

lead.purpose: Paragraph under section headings and in the hero, 52-58ch.

label.purpose: Form labels, filter chips, hero features; sentence case, never tracked uppercase.

caption.purpose: Placeholder labels, scale end labels, privacy note.

shadows.name: plank-selected

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system.

motion.name: reveal

motion.name: filter-pill

narrative.overview:
The site is a wood sampler, not a brochure. Dark roasted-wood grounds stand in for the dim workshop wall, and the real sample boards from the workshop (dąb, jesion, orzech amerykański, tatajuba, tauari) are the main evidence. They show up as cropped planks in a rack, in a horizontal rail and in a picker. Everything around them is held back: sharp rectangular frames like cut boards, 1px seams instead of cards, and numbers and dimensions treated like a joiner's pencil marks.

Density is calm and generous. Sections run full width inside a 1440px container, alternating between two near-black browns, so the eye reads one continuous dark surface split by grain, not a stack of boxes. Brass is the only warm accent. It marks every action and active state and almost nothing else. Cream is for headings and for the paper labels that the workshop sticks onto its samples, and the logo sits on one of those labels.

Honesty is part of the look. Stock imagery is allowed only with a visible "Zdjęcie poglądowe" (or "Poglądowe") tag. In the gallery it is also slightly dimmed and warmed, so it never passes for the workshop's own work.
keyCharacteristics: Espresso-to-walnut dark grounds, cream headings, sand body text, brass only for action.
Zero corner radius everywhere. Frames are cut boards.
1px seam lines and seam-filled grid gaps replace cards and boxes.
Real sample-board photos cropped into swatches carry the species story.
Cream paper labels (logo, gallery wood tags) as the one "applied" object on the surface.
Motion is restrained and starts from an already visible state. The one signature move is the species clip-path wipe.

rules.name: The Brass Means Act Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only on things you can press or on the current state (selected filter, selected species, filled scale segments). Decorative brass is limited to the small hero dash markers and list icons that sit beside actionable or factual rows. Brass is never a background for a section.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Page sections alternate espresso and umber. Walnut is used only for a contained panel (the form). Board is used only as an image well. No other surface colors.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Pencil Marks Rule
rules.body: Step numbers, phone numbers and hours are set in the display face (steps in brass, 600 at 1.5rem) or with `tabular-nums`. They work as measurements, not as decorative oversized numerals.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: h1–h3 use `text-wrap: balance` and paragraphs use `text-wrap: pretty`. Headings never break before a one-letter Polish preposition. Bind it with a non-breaking space.

rules.name: The Seam Not Card Rule
rules.body: Groups are divided by 1px seam lines, never boxed. Lists use a seam top border plus a seam bottom border on each row (O nas reasons, Kontakt details, mobile menu). Grid groups use a 1px gap over a seam-filled parent, so the seams appear between tiles (Oferta). Timelines use a seam left border on mobile and a seam top border on desktop (Jak pracujemy). The quote form is the only bordered panel, because it is a working surface.

rules.name: The Measuring Rule
rules.body: The tick-rule (1px seam ticks every 12px, 8px tall, fading out over its last 30%) sits under every section heading. It is the only ornamental line in the system.

rules.name: The Objects Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to things that could physically be picked up, such as labels and boards. Sections, panels, buttons and inputs cast no shadows.

rules.name: The Already Visible Rule
rules.body: Entrances never start from invisible. Section reveals go from opacity 0.6 and 18px down to rest (0.8s, once, triggered 10% before the viewport edge). Hero copy rises from opacity 0.35. Gallery tiles settle from opacity 0.3 at scale 0.98 when filters change. Content must stay readable if JavaScript or motion never runs. The single exception is the desktop hero rack (fading in from 0, 24px to the side), which is decorative because the same species are in the sampler.

rules.name: The One Signature Move Rule
rules.body: The clip-path wipe belongs to the species sampler alone. Elsewhere motion is limited to settling, image hover zoom (1.04–1.06 over 1.4–1.6s), color transitions and sliding sheets and bars.

dos: Do cut every frame square (0px) and divide groups with 1px seam (#4a392d) lines or seam-filled 1px gaps.
Do keep brass (#d4a373) for actions and current state. On hover, brass fills go to cream.
Do build species visuals from the real sample-board photos, cropped with `background-size` 320–400% at 58% 50% and a left espresso gradient behind cream names.
Do put the logo on a cream board label and tag gallery woods with cream labels in label-ink (#5a2e24).
Do tag every stock image "Zdjęcie poglądowe" (or "Poglądowe" on gallery tiles) in a dust caption on an espresso scrim, flush to a corner.
Do start entrances from an already visible state (opacity of at least 0.3) with ease-out-expo, and keep `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`.
Do follow every section h2 with the tick-rule and a sand lead.
Do bind Polish one-letter prepositions to the next word with a non-breaking space in headings.
donts: Don't wrap content in rounded or shadowed cards. The form panel is the only bordered container.
Don't use brass as a section background or as decoration on non-interactive surfaces.
Don't add shadows to buttons, inputs, sections or panels. Shadows are only for labels and planks.
Don't substitute flat color chips or generic wood textures for the real sample boards.
Don't show stock photography without the placeholder label, or present it as a realization.
Don't reuse the clip-path wipe outside the species sampler, or animate content in from opacity 0.
Don't set labels in tracked uppercase, and don't add small labels above section headings. The heading, tick-rule and lead sequence is the whole header.
